name: Omni Tucson National Resort & Spa
positioning: Desert golf and spa resort in Tucson near the Santa Catalina Mountains, with two championship golf courses, Mokara Spa and Southwestern-style casitas and suites
best_for: Golfers who want two championship courses on site
Families looking for pools, courts and organized resort activities
Couples wanting a suite with a fireplace and private patio

facts.text: The resort is in Tucson, near the Santa Catalina Mountains.
Tucson International Airport is about 20 miles, or about 35 minutes, away.
The resort has two championship golf courses.
The two courses are The Catalina and the Sonoran, and resort guests get discounted green fees on them.
The resort's full-service spa is Mokara Spa.
The resort has two pools, Sweet Water and Catalina.
Cabanas can be rented at the pools.
Deluxe Rooms have a private terrace or balcony.
The fitness center has Peloton bikes.
Family-friendly activities include games, hiking, biking and trivia nights.
Dining includes two full-service restaurants, a cafe, a lobby bar, a sports bar and a pool bar.
The on-site restaurants overlook the Catalina Mountains.

highlights.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes the resort's PGA schedule and its two courses by name designers Van Hagge/Devlin and Lehman.
The Hacienda Suite has championship golf or lush landscape views, a vaulted-ceiling living room, a fireplace, dining for four and a bedroom with a two-poster king bed.
The Casita Suite has a four-poster king bed, a fireplace, a private patio and doorstep parking.
The Catalina Activities Center has tennis and pickleball courts, sand volleyball and the Catalina Pool.
The Casitas are Southwestern inspired, with neutral tones and earthy textures.

considerations.text: The resort charges a $35 per night resort fee.
WhataHotel notes the secluded location means a car is needed to reach downtown Tucson attractions.
The resort is pet friendly for animals under 50 pounds.
